title: Cloudreve

tagline.en: Self-hosted cloud drive with file sharing, previews and multiple storage backends
tagline.es: Unidad en la nube autoalojada con uso compartido de archivos, vistas previas y varios backends de almacenamiento

tagline.hi: फ़ाइल साझाकरण, प्रीव्यू और कई स्टोरेज बैकएंड के साथ सेल्फ-होस्टेड क्लाउड ड्राइव

notes: The first account that signs up becomes the administrator (Cloudreve v4 has no default login). Open the site and sign up immediately after install.

Sign-ups stay open afterwards, and new accounts get the default "User" group with its storage quota. Once your own accounts exist, turn off registration in the Admin dashboard (Settings, Users), or keep it open on purpose.

The site's HTTPS address is seeded as Cloudreve's site URL on first start (CR_SETTING_DEFAULT_siteURL); download and share links are built from it. Cloudreve keeps that setting in its database, so if the domain changes later, update it in the Admin dashboard (Settings, Basic) as well.

Database and Redis settings use Cloudreve's CR_CONF_<Section>__<Key> overrides (the double-underscore form of the documented CR_CONF_<Section>.<Key>, so every variable name stays editable in the panel). PostgreSQL 17.11 (the official compose file's major version) uses a generated password instead of the official file's trust authentication; it and Redis 8.8 have their own volumes and no published port.
Uploaded files, thumbnails and conf.ini live in the data volume (/cloudreve/data, the default local storage policy). TZ is set to UTC: the image otherwise defaults to Asia/Shanghai.

Only the web port is published. The aria2 downloader for offline downloads runs inside the container, but its BitTorrent listen port (6888) is not exposed, so torrent downloads work without incoming peers.

The healthcheck calls /api/v4/site/ping with the image's busybox wget. The 1g floor leaves room for the thumbnail generators bundled in the image (LibreOffice, ffmpeg, libvips), which run inside the same container when previews are made.
Verified live on Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 (RC-31): created from the 1-Click Recipes tab, Running, HTTPS, first login and a real-use check passed; every image ref below is in its tested list.
